title: Copilot Cowork: access Business Applications through Work IQ and use business skills
summary: Hold: the checklist incorrectly treats turning off Work IQ as a way to stop Cowork reaching environment data, although Microsoft says participation settings do not prevent agentic access. The controls table also reports App Access automation as undocumented despite a documented Dataverse API for allowing or blocking applications.

claims.fix: Retain the cited Work IQ-specific path, but qualify its note: 'The general App Access documentation requires a managed environment and gives a different setup flow: Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/control-app-access-environment for that qualification.

claims.claim: An API for allowing or blocking applications' access to environment data is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /applications(applicationid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... Access ... LogicalName ... access ... Access Choices/Options ... 0 ... Allowed ... 1 ... Blocked
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].api null with kind 'rest', call 'PATCH https://<organization>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<applicationid>) with JSON body {"access":1}', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/application'. Qualify the note: 'The API changes an application's allowed/blocked status; configure environment-level App Access enforcement separately.' The documented access values are 0 for Allowed and 1 for Blocked.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, second bullet; Why it matters
claims.claim: Turning off the environment Work IQ setting prevents Cowork from reaching that environment's data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.
claims.fix: Replace the second Before rollout bullet with 'Check which environments have Work IQ turned on; use App Access Control to block Cowork from environments whose data it should not access.' Replace 'because they decide what Cowork can reach once the plugin is installed' in Why it matters with 'and separately review App Access Control for Cowork, because participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.' This also resolves the conflict with controls[2].note and the Governance controls notes.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The checklist's security-role reviews are represented by controls in the governance table.
claims.quote: Review Dataverse security roles in those environments ... Review who holds the Skill Sharing Role ... Controls rows cover plugin installation, audience, Work IQ features, App Access, spending and skill activation, but not security-role assignments.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step reviewing Dataverse security roles and the After rollout step reviewing Skill Sharing Role assignments have no corresponding control row. Do not add rows in this correction; remove those role-review clauses from the checklist, leaving their supported permission and role facts in Risk assessment.
